page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a large L3 cache of 480 MB, alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark data indicates average to strong performance characteristics. The CPU registers average tier results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as an average PassMark CPU score of 48743.5. However, single-threaded gzip compression is highly efficient, placing in the top tier at 36.05 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression shows strong performance at 180.33 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is measured at 146.04 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 62.52 GB/sec for write operations. For LLM inference, prompt processing on a medium 7B model is strong at 190.8 tokens/sec, though text generation on a large 70B model drops to a weak 2.69 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E32ds_v7 offers high resource density by combining a generous 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio with substantial local SSD storage. This configuration mitigates the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput local operations, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training. The instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, enterprise database systems, caching layers like Redis, data analytics, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
